question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed. Law 3.1 (laws-3.1, sentences 1 and 2) states the test stroke — a full underhand stroke contacting the shuttle over the back boundary line, hit at an upward angle parallel to the side lines — and Law 3.2 (laws-3.2, sentence 1) states the criterion for correct speed: the shuttle lands not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line (Diagram B). Together these answer the part. Related but not answering: itto-3.5.4.4 tells the Referee to consider how the shuttle was hit and from where when assessing the test; itto-3.6.3 has the Referee re-check the selected speed during play; itto-3.5.4.1 says who should test.
answer.answer: To test a shuttle for speed, a player shall use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line [1], and the shuttle shall be hit at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines [2]. A shuttle of correct speed will land not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line [3]. The shuttles should be tested by an active player in the tournament, preferably a male player, or a qualified person approved by the Referee [6]. When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit and whether they were hit from the correct location over the back line [4]. The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct [5].

answer.reasoning: The question asks two things: (1) whether a player whose string broke during a rally may change rackets mid-rally — answered directly by ITTO 5.10.1 sentence (2), 'A change of a racket at courtside during a rally is permitted'; and (2) whether the player may leave the court during play to get a replacement racket — answered by Law 16.5.2 (1) and ITTO 5.10.1 (1), which forbid leaving without the umpire's permission (causing delay) except during the Law 16.2 intervals, so the interval rules Law 16.2.1 (1) and Law 16.2.2 (1) complete that part. The Alternative Laws 16.2 chunks are for non-standard formats not in force and are not needed for this standard-play question.
answer.answer: A change of racket at courtside during a rally is permitted [1]. You must not leave the court during a match without the umpire's permission, and you must not cause delay to play, except during the allowed intervals [2][3]. Those intervals are not exceeding 60 seconds during each game when the leading score reaches 11 points, except Handicap matches [4], and not exceeding 120 seconds between the first and second game and between the second and third game [5]. Under no circumstances shall play be delayed to enable you to recover strength or wind or to receive advice [6]. The umpire will prevent any unnecessary walk around the court between rallies and testing of replacement rackets on court, and if necessary Law 16.7 shall be applied [7].
